global_field_rules.availability: Price/macro rows at or before snapshot label. SEC facts require filed and end dates <= snapshot and finite values. Events require filingDate <= snapshot. No download-vintage guarantee.

market_prices.selection: 14 investable columns; <= snapshot, ffill, drop incomplete rows; require >=253 rows

valuation_and_adv.basis: Yahoo quote close, dividend-unadjusted and split-adjusted to recorded corporate-action cutoff

instant_fact_selection.namespaces: shares: us-gaap then dei candidates pooled; other instant values: us-gaap

global_field_rules.shares: Selected instant shares; if absent, latest annual diluted/basic weighted-average shares. As-filed shares multiplied by all split factors strictly after shares period end through recorded action cutoff.
global_field_rules.safe_ratio: NA if operand missing, abs(denominator)<=1e-12, or result non-finite; P/E additionally requires positive net income.
global_field_rules.event_history: SEC recent plus all archived filing tables; deduplicate tuple(accessionNumber,filingDate,form,primaryDocument); sort(filingDate,accessionNumber). Latest filingDate tie keeps first row.

risk_reference.prices: all 50 adjusted-close columns, <= snapshot, ffill, last 253 rows

global_field_rules.packet_order: RESEARCH PACKET newline; ticker | asset headers; 14 asset rows; optional final market context | macro label=value pairs. Asset and macro subsequences preserve frozen field order. Shared uses registry order.

prompt_template:
You are an institutional U.S. equity analyst. Construct a one-month active long/short book that seeks the best expected risk-adjusted return from the supplied evidence. Do not create different positions merely to appear diversified.

You receive one packet from a research workflow. Its field composition was fixed before model collection. Use only the supplied packet. Do not infer missing fields, import current facts, or use outside knowledge. The calendar date is intentionally hidden.

COMMON UNIVERSE
{snapshot['common_core']}

PERMITTED INFORMATION
{packet_text}

Give every listed ticker a signed conviction score from -1 to +1, with both positive and negative scores. Positive means long and negative means short. These are research scores, not final capital weights. The fixed evaluation pipeline subtracts their mean and rescales absolute exposure to 1, imposing the same dollar-neutral book construction on every response.

Reply with one JSON object and no markdown. The weights field must be an object containing every listed ticker exactly once. Use this schema: {"weights":{"{example}":0.10,"...":0.00},"thesis":"at most 35 words","primary_signals":["signal 1","signal 2"]}}.

request.seed: Included only for catalog seed support. 2026072100 + int(SHA256(date|architecture|team_size|packet_index|vendor)[:7],16) % 100000000 + applicable recovery offset

historical_prompt_typo: The literal textual example ends with ]}}. (one excess closing brace); retained verbatim. The actual response_format schema is well-formed and distinct.
runtime_constraint_boundary: Schema requires all ticker-number properties and thesis/primary_signals; it has no score bounds, thesis word count, or signal count. Collector checks finite complete nonconstant scores and abs(score)<=1+1e-12; mixed signs and 35-word thesis are prompt-only constraints.
